how.title: Four steps from forgotten archive to a new beginning.

s1.title: Upload
s1.text: Add a PDF report, Markdown notes or a code folder tree, after your team agrees.

s2.title: Verify
s2.text: AI drafts the unfinished tasks. You keep, edit or remove each one before anything is public.

s3.title: Continue
s3.text: A team reads the teaser, then takes access right away or sends a short plan, as the owners chose.

s4.title: Continue with credit
s4.text: Each person who continues accepts the attribution agreement. Private files open and the lineage is logged.

g1.title: Every task cites its source
g1.text: Each drafted task links to a page or file, and ESTAFET checks that the quoted text really exists there.

g2.title: Nothing public until verified
g2.text: Publishing stays blocked until the owners have reviewed every drafted item.

g3.title: Team consent first
g3.text: Every team member has to confirm before the files are read by AI and before a project can be published.

delete.title: Delete my account
delete.intro: Deletion has a 30 day waiting period so you can change your mind. During that time you can still sign in and cancel it. This is what happens when the waiting period ends:
delete.l1: Your profile becomes “Pengguna lama” (former user): name, university, faculty and photo are removed. Your email address is released and the account can no longer sign in.
delete.l2: Pending requests to continue are withdrawn. Your access to other people's projects ends. Notifications and your “Notify me” list are deleted.
delete.l3: Draft projects that only you own are deleted together with their files.
delete.l4: Projects that are published, unpublished or archived stay, with the owner shown as “Pengguna lama”, so teams who continued them keep a correct attribution line. If you do not want such a project to be shown, unpublish it before the waiting period ends.
delete.l5: Reports you sent stay for moderation records, without a link to your account. Records of accepted terms and project lineage entries are kept.
delete.scheduled: Your account is scheduled for deletion on {date}. You can cancel it before then.
delete.confirmTitle: Schedule the deletion of your account?
delete.confirmEffect: Your account is scheduled to be deleted 30 days from now. You can still sign in and cancel until then. After that, deletion cannot be undone.
delete.failed: The deletion could not be scheduled. Please try again.

terms.title: Terms and Conditions
terms.lead: ESTAFET helps student teams hand over discontinued competition and research projects to the next team. By using ESTAFET you agree to these terms.

s1.p: Anyone can browse projects without an account. To share a project or take access you need an account with a confirmed email. One account can both share and continue projects. You are responsible for keeping your password safe.

s2.p: You may share only a project you worked on and whose files you have the right to share. Every active team member must agree. Do not upload secrets (passwords, API keys), other people's personal data, or files you may not share. The public summary shows only what you reviewed and approved.

s3.p: Project files are not shown on public pages. Only the owners and people who hold access can open them. Owners choose whether access is open, by request, or paused.

s4.p: Anyone who takes access must accept the Attribution Agreement and credit the original owners in work built on it. Access can be revoked by the owners or the ESTAFET team with a written reason. The attribution duty stays after access is revoked.

s5.p: Anyone can report a project. The ESTAFET team can hold, hide or remove a project from public view based on the Community Guidelines. Every decision comes with a written reason, and owners can appeal once per decision. Moderation does not delete data, and agreements already accepted do not change.

s6.p: You can ask for an AI draft or fill everything in by hand. An AI draft is a suggestion: you review, edit or remove every item before publishing. You are responsible for what you publish.

s7.p: ESTAFET is a student project and is provided as is. We do not guarantee that the service is always available or error free, or that the content users share is accurate.

s8.p: If the terms change, we publish a new version and ask you to accept it again before you continue. We record the version you accepted and when.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.lead: This page explains what data ESTAFET stores, what for, and what you can do with it.

s1.p: Account: name, email address, and university or faculty if you give them. Projects: the details you enter and the files you upload. Access and requests: who holds access to which project, and the messages in requests. Reports and appeals. Notifications. A record of which version of the terms and policies you accepted, and when.

s2.p: Data is kept in the database and file storage service ESTAFET uses (Supabase). Project files sit in private storage and are opened only through short-lived links after a permission check.

s3.p: If you ask for an AI draft, the text of the files you choose is sent to the AI provider ESTAFET is configured to use. Every team member must agree first. Source code is not sent apart from the README and package manifests. You can decline: choose “Fill in by hand without AI” and nothing is sent.

s4.p: The identity of a reporter is never shown to the project owners. Reports from guests store only a hashed form of the network address to limit abuse, not the address itself.

s5.p: We use only essential cookies: your sign-in session and your language choice. We do not use advertising or tracking cookies.

s6.p: You can download a copy of your data (JSON) and ask for your account to be deleted from the Account privacy page. Deletion has a 30 day waiting period. After it, your profile becomes “Pengguna lama” (former user). Published projects stay without your name so teams that continued them keep a correct attribution line, unless you unpublish them before the waiting period ends.

s7.p: Account data is kept while your account exists. Records of accepted terms, lineage entries and moderation audit entries are kept longer because they serve as evidence. Technical logs do not contain file contents or personal data.

s8.p: Questions about personal data? See the Contact page.

guidelines.title: Community Guidelines
guidelines.lead: The ESTAFET team uses these rules to judge reports. They keep shared projects honest, safe and owned by people who have the right to share them.

s1.p: Do not share work that is not yours or that you may not share, such as other people's reports, closed-license code or paid material.

s2.p: Do not share other people's personal data without permission: ID numbers, addresses, private contacts, grades or research participant data.

s3.p: Do not write summaries, results or evidence you know are untrue. Show what was really finished and what was not.

s4.p: No content that harasses, threatens, spreads hatred, or is unfit for an academic setting.

s5.p: Do not claim to own or to have been on the team of a project that is not yours.

s6.p: Do not upload files that contain malware, passwords, secret keys or anything designed to cause harm.

s7.p: Do not use ESTAFET for advertising, unrelated links or pointless mass uploads.

s8.p: The team reads every report. If several different reporters report something serious (copyright, personal data, harmful files), the project is held for review. A hold is not a finding that a rule was broken. Every decision (dismiss, hold, hide, remove, restore) has a written reason. Owners receive the reason and can appeal once. Reporters' identities are never shown to owners.

attribution.title: Attribution Agreement
attribution.lead: Everyone who takes access to a project's files accepts this agreement. It is a simple template for student projects.

s1.p: You credit the original owners by name in any submission, paper or product page that builds on this project. The owners state they have the right to share the files. Ownership of the original work stays with its owners, and your new work belongs to you. ESTAFET records the handover in the lineage.

s2.p: Every project has a credit line you can copy from the project room, with the title, the owners' names and the lineage code.

s3.p: The agreement has a version number. Your acceptance is recorded with its version. If a new version is published, projects you already took stay under the version you accepted.

s4.p: The owners or the ESTAFET team can revoke your access with a written reason. The attribution duty stays for work you already made with help from that project.

s5.p: This is a simple template for student projects and is not legal advice. Check your university's rules for shared work.
